facts.statement: ipv4: free inet_opt and ireq_opt after an RCU grace period
CVE-2026-98432 is a flaw in how the Linux kernel sets up IPv4 TCP connections
root on a Linux server with a multipath TCP (MPTCP) listener, with no credentials and no user interaction.
Install a patched kernel and reboot.
Vendors backport fixes, so use their own fixed version rather than the upstream one.

editorial.title: Linux TCP flaw puts exposed hosts on the kernel patch list
editorial.summary: CVE-2026-98432 affects Linux IPv4 TCP connection handling. Aikido reports a demonstrated remote-root exploit against an MPTCP listener; that condition should guide urgent exposure checks without being treated as the full boundary of the flaw.
editorial.why_it_matters: The Linux CNA describes a memory-lifetime bug with potential control-flow corruption. Check reachable IPv4 services and MPTCP listeners when prioritizing hosts.
editorial.action: Install your distribution’s patched kernel, reboot, and verify the running kernel against its advisory. Use vendor backport guidance rather than comparing only upstream version numbers.
